results.title: Grain API
results.snippet:
# Authentication
Grain supports three authentication methods depending on your use case.
**Personal Access Token (PAT)**: grants access on behalf of a single user. The token has the same permissions as the user who generated it. Best for personal automations or testing. Available on every plan, including Free. Click [here](https://grain.com/app/settings/account/integrations/personal_api) to generate a PAT.
**Workspace Access Token (WAT)**: grants access to all data in the workspace, regardless of which user owns it. Use this for server-side integrations where you need workspace-wide access. Requires admin access to generate and is available on Business and Enterprise plans. Click [here](https://grain.com/app/settings/integrations?tab=api) to generate a WAT.
**OAuth2**: the standard flow for building integrations to be used by any Grain user. Users authorize your application directly, and your app receives a token scoped to that user's data. Required if you are building an integration to distribute to others.

results.title: Authentication — Grain Developers
results.snippet:
To authenticate API calls, the client must add the following header:
```javascript
Authorization: Bearer TOKEN
```
where `TOKEN` is obtained by one of the methods below.
## Token Types
There are three types of tokens which can have one of two access scopes.
| **Type** | **Scope** | |
|---|---|---|
| Personal Access Token (`PAT`) | `personal` | Generated manually from the [integrations page](https://grain.com/app/settings/account/integrations/personal_api). Doesn't expire, and can be revoked at any time. |
| Workspace Access Token (`WAT`) | `workspace` | Generated manually from the [integrations page](https://grain.com/app/settings/integrations?tab=api). Doesn't expire, and can be revoked at any time. |
| OAuth Token | `personal`, `workspace` | Issued through the OAuth2 Flow. Expires, must be refreshed. |
| **Scope** | |
|---|---|
| `personal` | Provides the same access level as the user who authorized the token. |
| `workspace` | Provides **FULL DATA ACCESS** of the workspace. Can be generated by workspace admins only. |
> **NOTE:** The `workspace` scope is not available on all plans.
> Check [https://grain.com/pricing](https://grain.com/pricing) to see if your plan includes Worksp

results.title: Overview — Grain Developers
results.snippet:
### 1. Create a Personal Access Token
A Personal Access Token (PAT) authenticates requests as you, with the same access you have in Grain. Generate one here:
See [Authentication](https://developers.grain.com/authentication.html) for the other ways to authenticate.
### 2. Make Your First Request
Every request needs a token in the `Authorization` header and a `Public-Api-Version` header (see [Versions](https://developers.grain.com/versions.html)).
Here's [Token Info](https://developers.grain.com/endpoints.html#token-info), using an example token:
```bash
curl -X GET \
-H "Authorization: Bearer grain_pat_example123" \
-H "Public-Api-Version: 2026-10-01" \
https://api.grain.com/_/public-api/v2/token-info
```
```json
{
"type": "personal_access_token",
"scope": "personal",
"user_id": "7890-abcd-ef01-2222-3456-7890ffff",
"name": "Luke Skywalker",
"expires_at": null
}
```
Swap in your own token and you're set.

Grain supports three token types (see the [API docs](https://developers.grain.com/#authentication)):
| Type | Scope | Where to get it |
|---|---|---|
| **Personal Access Token (PAT)** | acts as you | [https://grain.com/app/settings/integrations?tab=api](https://grain.com/app/settings/integrations?tab=api) |
| **Workspace Access Token (WAT)** | all workspace data | same page (needs workspace access) |
| **OAuth2** | acts as the authorizing user | register a client with Grain |
### Store a token
```
grain auth login                     # prompts for a token (hidden input), stores a PAT
grain auth login --type wat          # store a Workspace token
grain auth login --token grain_pat_… # non-interactive
echo "$TOKEN" | grain auth login     # from a pipe / secret manager
```
### OAuth2 (Authorization Code + PKCE)
```
grain auth login --oauth \
--client-id YOUR_CLIENT_ID \
--client-secret YOUR_SECRET \
--redirect-uri http://localhost:8976/callback
```
This opens your browser, runs the loopback flow, and stores the access + refresh tokens. Expired access tokens are refreshed automatically before each command.
### Inspect / rotate
```
grain auth status          # show the resolved profile

results.title: Export meetings
results.snippet:
**Personal API token**
Any user, on every plan including Free, can generate a personal token to access meetings they have permission to view.
1. Go to 'Account settings' → 'Integrations' → 'Personal API'.
2. Click 'Generate personal API token'.
**Workspace API token (admins only)**
Workspace admins on Business and Enterprise plans can generate a token with access to all meetings across the workspace.
1. Go to 'Workspace settings' → 'Integrations' → 'API'.
2. Click 'Generate workspace API token'.
What you can extract:
- Transcripts
- MP4 recordings
Rate limit: ~300 API calls per minute.

results.title: Release notes
results.snippet:
Plan availability:
Free
Starter

**Recording consent**
Grain can now ask attendees for consent before it records. Attendees get an email 24 hours before the meeting and can approve or decline. If anyone declines, Grain won't auto-record that meeting, and you'll get an email each time someone responds. Admins can turn this feature on in Workspace Settings > General and choose which meetings and attendees get the request. Available on Business and Enterprise plans. [Learn more](https://support.grain.com/en/articles/17218482-recording-consent)
**API improvements**
We've made big improvements to our API and its documentation. A few highlights:
- Much more reliable uploads for audio, video, or transcripts only
- Metadata you can edit through the API
- Access and sharing controls at upload
- Much easier querying
Check out the [new API documentation](https://developers.grain.com/overview.html).
**8-hour meeting limit**
Meetings on Business workspaces can now run up to 8 hours, up from 4. The limit is still 4 hours on Starter and 45 minutes on Free.

results.title: Grain API
results.snippet:
The Grain API lets developers read meeting data, manage recordings, and receive real-time events from Grain programmatically. Use it to build custom integrations, sync data to internal systems, or automate workflows that go beyond what Grain's built-in integrations support.
# What you can do with the API
**Read meeting data**: retrieve recordings, transcripts, AI notes and action items, participants, tags, teams, and meeting types from your workspace.
**Manage recordings**: upload external recordings to Grain, update recording metadata, add or remove tags, and control sharing at the user or team level.
**Download recordings**: export video files and transcripts in multiple formats (JSON, plain text, VTT, SRT) for archiving or processing.
**Receive real-time events**: register webhooks to receive a payload whenever a new recording is processed in your workspace, so downstream systems stay in sync without polling.

results.title: Notion
results.snippet:
Each Custom Agent needs its own connection to Grain, this is not a workspace-wide integration. The connection runs on the credentials of whoever set it up.
MCP connections for Custom Agents are available on Notion Business and Enterprise plans only. Grain isn't in Notion's list of pre-configured connections, so you'll connect it as a custom MCP server.
---
## Turn on custom MCP servers for your workspace
A workspace admin has to enable custom MCP servers before anyone can connect Grain to an agent.
1. As a workspace admin, go to 'Settings', then 'Connections'.
2. In the 'Manage' tab, toggle on 'Enable custom MCP servers'.
3. Optionally, add Grain's MCP server URL to your workspace's approved connections list so members don't need individual admin approval to add it.
**Note:** *If your workspace limits members to admin-approved connections only, add Grain's server URL under 'Approved connections' before anyone tries to connect it to an agent.*
---
## Connect Grain to a Custom Agent
Do this for each Custom Agent that needs Grain data.
1. Open the Custom Agent's 'Settings'.
2. Go to 'Tools & Access'.
3. Select 'Add connection', then 'Custom MCP server'.
4. Enter Grain's MCP server URL

results.title: Claude
results.snippet:
Grain is available as a native connector in Claude. Once connected, you can ask about a meeting the same way you'd ask Claude anything else, and Claude pulls the transcript, AI notes, action items, or other Grain data behind the scenes.
---
## Connect Grain to Claude
1. In Claude, go to ’Customize’ → ‘Connectors’
2. Click '+' to search for connectors
3. Search for ‘Grain’
4. Select & connect Grain
5. You’ll be redirected to Grain to approve the connection

## How Grain surfaces inside Claude
Once Grain is connected to Claude via MCP you can pull up action items, summarize a call, or search across meetings for a topic, a company, or a person. Claude can also create clips, tag meetings, build a playlist from a set of meetings, or pull together a story from clips.
On Grain Business and Enterprise plans, Claude can pull HubSpot deal intelligence, sales coaching scorecards, and multi-meeting analyses like SPICED or MEDDICC qualification, either from a plain-language request or from a library of pre-built report prompts that chain several Grain lookups into a single structured report.

**Can Claude take actions in Grain, or just read data?** That depends on which Grain tools you enable.
